name: Logitech MX Master 3S
multiDevice: 3 hosts (Bluetooth or Logi Bolt), Easy-Switch button + Flow cross-computer
notes: Best-in-class MagSpeed electromagnetic wheel with SmartShift auto-ratchet; quiet clicks; tracks on glass; not for fast gaming.

name: Logitech MX Master 4
multiDevice: 3 hosts (Bluetooth or Logi Bolt), Easy-Switch button + Flow cross-computer
notes: Adds haptic feedback motor, extra thumb button and an Action Ring context menu over the MX Master 3S; same MagSpeed wheel.

name: Logitech MX Anywhere 3S
multiDevice: 3 hosts (Bluetooth or Logi Bolt), Easy-Switch button + Flow
notes: Compact travel version of the MX line with the same MagSpeed ratchet/free-spin wheel; no dedicated thumb wheel.

name: Logitech MX Vertical
multiDevice: 3 hosts (Bluetooth or Unifying), Easy-Switch button + Flow
notes: 57-degree vertical handshake grip to reduce wrist pronation; plain notched wheel, no free-spin.

name: Logitech MX Ergo S
notes: Thumb-operated ball on an adjustable 0/20-degree tilt plate; quieter clicks and USB-C vs original MX Ergo; precision-speed button.

name: Logitech ERGO M575S
multiDevice: 2 hosts (1 Bolt dongle + 1 Bluetooth), manual pairing switch
notes: Entry thumb trackball; no wired mode, no tilt, no free-spin - just a dependable notched wheel.

name: Logitech Lift Vertical Ergonomic Mouse
multiDevice: 3 hosts (Bolt or Bluetooth), Easy-Switch button + Flow
notes: Smaller-handed alternative to MX Vertical at 58 degrees; left-handed version sold separately; no wired mode.

name: Logitech Signature M650 L
notes: Budget silent-click ergo mouse; SmartWheel gives light near-free spin under fast flicks but has no true free-spin mode.

name: Keychron M6 Wireless
priceNote: ~$40 for PixArt 3395 1K version, ~$60 for 8K PixArt 3950 version
notes: Lightweight tri-mode with silent-switch option and 5 onboard profiles; software-free web configurator.

name: ProtoArc EM01 NL
notes: Budget thumb trackball with adjustable 20-degree tilt and RGB; wireless only, no software remapping.

name: MCHOSE AX5 Pro Max
notes: Budget lightweight tri-mode gaming mouse; frequent value pick, build and software less polished than majors.

name: Kensington SlimBlade Pro
multiDevice: 1 Bluetooth + 1 dongle host, mode switch (no rapid multi-host switching)
notes: Large 55mm finger ball; scrolling is done by twisting the ball itself; 4 corner buttons, no thumb buttons.

name: Kensington Expert Mouse Wireless
notes: Iconic 55mm center ball with a physical scroll ring around it; ambidextrous; 4 corner buttons, wrist rest included.

name: Kensington Pro Fit Ergo Vertical Wireless Trackball
notes: Vertical thumb-ball trackball at a 60-degree angle; 9 programmable buttons and true 3-device switching.

name: Kensington Orbit Fusion Wireless Trackball
notes: Finger-operated 40mm ball with scroll ring and detachable wrist rest; 2.4GHz only, no Bluetooth.

name: Elecom HUGE (M-HT1DRBK)
notes: Large 52mm thumb ball with a big palm rest, 8 buttons, tilt wheel and adjustable click tension; 2.4GHz only.

name: Elecom DEFT Pro (M-DPT1MRBK)
notes: Index/middle-finger 52mm ball, 8 buttons plus tilt wheel; one of the few Elecom balls with wired + BT + dongle.

name: Elecom EX-G Pro Trackball (M-XPT1MRBK)
notes: Compact thumb-ball with 8 buttons, tilt wheel and tri-mode connectivity; supports low click-noise switches.

name: Ploopy Classic Trackball
notes: Open-source, 3D-printed, QMK-programmable finger trackball; fully remappable firmware, optical encoder scroll.

name: Razer Basilisk V3
notes: Wired HyperScroll wheel with a physical toggle between tactile and free-spin plus tilt; sniper button on thumb.

name: Razer Basilisk V3 Pro
multiDevice: none (game-focused; one active link at a time)
notes: Wireless HyperScroll Tilt wheel with tactile / free-spin / Smart-Reel auto modes; optional wireless charging dock.

name: Razer Basilisk V3 Pro 35K
multiDevice: none (game-focused; one active link at a time)
notes: Spec-bump of the V3 Pro: 35K Gen-2 sensor, native 8K wireless polling, longer battery; same HyperScroll Tilt wheel.

name: Razer DeathAdder V3 Pro
notes: Lightweight esports ergo shape; no Bluetooth, plain notched wheel, minimal buttons - built for FPS.

name: Razer DeathAdder V4 Pro
notes: Lighter DeathAdder with 45K sensor and built-in 8K polling; still FPS-minimal, no BT or free-spin.

name: Razer Viper V3 Pro
notes: Ultralight ambidextrous esports mouse (right-side buttons only); pure competitive tool, no BT.

name: Razer Naga V2 Pro
multiDevice: Bluetooth + HyperSpeed dongle; swap side plates (2/6/12 button)
notes: Flagship MMO mouse: swappable 2/6/12-button thumb plates plus HyperScroll tilt toggle wheel.

name: Razer Naga V2 HyperSpeed
notes: AA-powered 12-side-button MMO mouse with HyperScroll toggle wheel; no wired mode, fixed side plate.

name: Razer Pro Click V2 Vertical Edition
multiDevice: 4 hosts (1 HyperSpeed dongle + 3 Bluetooth), Easy-Switch button
notes: Razer's productivity vertical mouse; genuine multi-host switching across four devices, silent clicks.

name: Razer Pro Click V2
multiDevice: 4 hosts (1 HyperSpeed dongle + 3 Bluetooth), Easy-Switch button
notes: Productivity ergo with a free-spin toggle wheel plus tilt and true 4-device switching - a rare Razer MX Master rival.

name: Logitech G502 X Plus
notes: Loaded wireless gaming mouse: dual-mode scroll with manual free-spin toggle, tilt, removable DPI-shift button, LIGHTFORCE switches.

name: Logitech G502 X Lightspeed
notes: Same as G502 X Plus without RGB; keeps the physical ratchet/free-spin toggle and tilt wheel.

name: Logitech G Pro X Superlight 2
notes: Minimalist ultralight esports mouse; right-side buttons present but not sculpted; plain wheel, no BT.

name: Logitech G303 Shroud Edition
notes: Revived angular G303 shape tuned with pro Shroud; light and fast, no free-spin or BT.

name: Logitech G309 Lightspeed
battery: AA x1, up to 300h (600h BT); POWERPLAY compatible
notes: Value Lightspeed mouse; AA battery, adds Bluetooth so it doubles as a light productivity mouse.

name: Logitech G604 Lightspeed
battery: AA x1, up to 240h (5.5 months BT)
notes: Lightweight-MMO hybrid with six thumb buttons and a MagSpeed-style ratchet/free-spin toggle wheel; AA powered.

name: Logitech G600 MMO Gaming Mouse
notes: Classic 12-button thumb-grid MMO mouse with a third 'G-Shift' ring finger button; tilt wheel, no free-spin.

name: Corsair Scimitar Elite Wireless SE
notes: 12-button slider thumb pad that physically adjusts fore/aft; SE adds an Elgato virtual Stream Deck integration.

name: Corsair M75 Air Wireless
notes: Ultralight symmetrical mouse; swappable left/right side buttons; plain wheel, no tilt.

name: Corsair Dark Core RGB Pro SE
battery: up to 50h rechargeable (Qi wireless charging on SE)
notes: Wide ergo palm mouse with interchangeable side grips; SE model supports Qi wireless charging.

name: SteelSeries Aerox 5 Wireless
notes: Holey lightweight mouse with a multi-directional thumb-button cluster (9 inputs) and tilt wheel; IP54 rated.

name: SteelSeries Aerox 9 Wireless
notes: Lightest 12-side-button MMO mouse thanks to a honeycomb shell; IP54 water/dust resistant; tilt wheel.

name: SteelSeries Prime Wireless
notes: Pure FPS mouse designed with pros; magnetic optical switches, no BT, plain wheel.

name: Glorious Model O 2 Wireless
notes: Lightweight symmetrical shape (right-side buttons only); adds Bluetooth over the original Model O.

name: Glorious Model I 2 Wireless
notes: MMO-lite with two removable/reconfigurable thumb buttons over a 4-button base (up to 6 side inputs).

name: ASUS ROG Harpe Ace Aim Lab Edition
notes: Ultralight esports mouse co-developed with Aim Lab; right-side buttons only, plain wheel.

name: ASUS ROG Keris II Ace
notes: Lightweight ergo shape with hot-swappable switch sockets; SpeedNova wireless with 8K option.

name: ASUS ROG Chakram X
battery: up to 130h rechargeable, USB-C, Qi charging
notes: Feature-maximal mouse with a detachable analog joystick on the thumb, hot-swap switches and 8K wireless polling.

name: Endgame Gear XM2we
notes: Lightweight low-profile ergo favored for its shape and neutral clicks; AAA-powered, no BT.

name: Pulsar X2V3 Wireless
priceNote: MSRP; ~$95 for standard, more for Premium/8K
notes: Ultralight symmetrical esports mouse with swappable side buttons and grip covers; no Bluetooth.

name: Lamzu Maya X
notes: Sub-50g ergo enthusiast mouse; premium sensor and switches, minimal buttons, no BT.

name: Vaxee XE Wireless
notes: Driverless enthusiast mouse tuned for feel and click latency; no software, no BT, plain wheel.

name: Zowie EC2-CW
notes: Plug-and-play CS competitive mouse; all settings on the underside, no software, no BT, DPI capped low by design.

name: Ninjutso Sora V2
notes: One of the lightest production wireless mice at ~39g; symmetrical, no BT, enthusiast-focused.

name: UtechSmart Venus Pro Wireless
notes: Budget 12-button MMO with tri-mode connectivity and 3-device switching; the value pick versus Naga/Scimitar.
